newsitem.title: USA: Giscard d'Estaing sees Italy, Spain in Euro.
newsitem.headline: Giscard d'Estaing sees Italy, Spain in Euro.

text.p: Former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing said on Thursday that he expected that both Italy and Spain would meet financial targets sufficiently in order to join European monetary union in the first wave.
"If Italy goes on with the effort (to meet fiscal goals), they will qualify for monetary union," Giscard d'Estaing said in a speech at Georgetown University.
Spain's economic situation was better than Italy's, and it was also likely to qualify, he told Reuters afterwards.
He also said it would not be desirable to have one of the two countries join without the other.

In his speech, Giscard d'Estaing said that, under the Maastricht Treaty, the financial targets were not completely rigid and that there was room for interpretation by the Council of Ministers on which countries were ultimately eligible.
He also said that future monetary policy was the key to allaying German fears that the Euro might not prove to be as stable a currency as the mark.
"The definition of future monetary policy ... is something which has not been addressed up to now sufficiently," he said.

He also said that more thought was needed on democratic accountability of a proposed European central bank, which he said was in danger of "being independent but not knowing what it is independent from."
